why: Brackets must close in the reverse order they opened, which is last-in first-out: push each opener and, at each closer, the top of the stack must be its matching opener.
hints: Which open bracket must the next closing bracket match?
The most recent unmatched opener. Keep openers on a stack; a closer pops the top and must be the same type.
One pass with a list as stack and a dict mapping closer -> opener; valid if no mismatch occurs and the stack is empty at the end. O(n).
pitfalls: A closer with an empty stack (")(") is invalid.
Leftover openers at the end ("((") make the string invalid.
Matching counts per type is not enough: "([)]" has balanced counts but is invalid.
statement:
Given a string s made only of the characters ( ) [ ] { }, return true if it is valid and false otherwise.

A string is valid when:

  • every opening bracket is closed by a bracket of the same type,
  • brackets are closed in the reverse order in which they were opened, and
  • every closing bracket has an earlier opening bracket to match.

The empty string is valid.

Worked example: s = "([)]"

  • (: open, pending openers (
  • [: open, pending ( [
  • ): the most recent opener is [, not (, so the string is invalid.

Answer: false. For "()[]{}" each opener is closed immediately by its partner, so the answer is true; for "{[]}" the answer is also true.
constraints:
• 0 <= s.length <= 10^4
  • s contains only the characters ( ) [ ] { }
  • Bounds are not stated in the source (an interview report); these are the standard LeetCode 20 bounds.
